source.title: Palladium-catalyzed 1,4-Addition of Terminal Alkynes to Conjugated Enones

reaction.notes: First step only: Pd(OAc)2/PMe3-catalyzed 1,4-addition of phenylacetylene to ethyl vinyl ketone in water; staged alkyne addition; 60 °C for 48 h.
reaction.tags: palladium; conjugate addition; alkyne; enone; water; PMe3; biphasic; vigorous stirring

conditions.atmosphere: N2; dissolve Pd(OAc)2 and PMe3 (homogeneous brown)
Add DI water (biphasic); N2 no longer required
Add phenylacetylene (0.6 equiv) then ethyl vinyl ketone (1.5 equiv); vigorous stirring ~1400 rpm
Add remaining phenylacetylene (0.4 equiv) at 0.4 mL/min
Heat in oil bath; vigorous stirring; darkening to dark brown

workup: Cool to room temperature; transfer to separatory funnel.
Wash combined organics with saturated brine (3 × 5 mL).
Dry over anhydrous Na2SO4 (25 g, 8 h).
Filter and concentrate at 200 mmHg then 10 mmHg at 25 °C.

purification.eluent: Hexanes/EtOAc: 50:1 to remove byproduct; then 15:1 to elute product (total ~500 mL)
purification.fractions: Analyze by TLC (10% EtOAc/hexanes); combine product fractions; optional vacuum distillation (120 °C/1 mmHg)

notes: Byproduct 1,4-diphenyl-1,3-butadiyne observed in early fractions (~4% yield).
Isolated product 7-phenyl-6-heptyn-3-one as brown liquid 6.85–6.94 g (75%); after distillation colorless liquid 6.20 g (66%).

original_procedure: In a 100-mL three-necked flask under N2, Pd(OAc)2 and PMe3 (1.0 M in toluene) are stirred 10 min to give a brown solution. Add deionized water (50 mL), then phenylacetylene (0.6 equiv) and ethyl vinyl ketone (1.5 equiv). With vigorous stirring (~1400 rpm), add the remaining phenylacetylene (0.4 equiv) at 0.4 mL/min. Heat at 60 °C for 48 h, then extract with ether, wash with brine, dry (Na2SO4), concentrate, and purify by silica gel column; optional short-path distillation affords the product. [Paraphrased from the source page.]
